folder: data/, chunks/, storage/, logs/, outputs/, bvb_scraped_data/
title: Data directories, indexes & artifacts
purpose: This subsystem holds every non-code data artifact the campus helpdesk produces or consumes: the raw scraped website corpus (bvb_scraped_data/), the cleaned canonical Markdown knowledge source (data/canonical_markdown/), the built FAISS/BM25 retrieval indexes (data/faiss/, chunks/), the Piper TTS voice model (data/piper/), and the runtime/observability outputs (logs/, storage/snapshots/, outputs/, data/analytics/reports/). It is the 'ground truth' layer: the ingestion pipeline (campus_helpdesk.ingest / canonical_index_builder) reads canonical Markdown to build the vector index that hybrid_retriever queries at /chat time, while the evaluation benchmark (bvb_scraped_data/benchmark/) is the ground-truth Q&A set used to score retrieval and answer quality. The bvb_scraped_data/ tree is a separate Node.js build system (scripts/*.mjs) that converts 4700+ raw crawled pages into a deduplicated knowledge_base corpus; nothing in the Python runtime imports it directly.

files.purpose: Sidecar manifest for the production FAISS vector index, recording the embedding model and normalization flag used to build it.

terms.definition: A small JSON sidecar that records how an index was built (embedding model name, normalize flag) so loaders can validate the on-disk index before deserializing it.
The sentence-transformer model (here sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2) that maps text to dense vectors used for similarity search.
Whether vectors are L2-normalized before storage, which makes cosine similarity equivalent to dot product in FAISS.

files.notes: Only 90 bytes: {"embedding_model": "sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2", "embedding_normalize": true}. Validated by faiss_store.py before loading index.pkl. Settings default embedding_normalize=true, matching this manifest.

files.purpose: Binary FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) vector index of ~11MB containing the dense embeddings for all knowledge chunks.

terms.definition: A binary index structure (faiss.read_index) supporting fast approximate nearest-neighbor search over the chunk embeddings; here the dense arm of the hybrid retriever.

files.notes: Binary file (~11MB), written by the ingest/index-builder and read by faiss_store.py at startup; built 2026-08-05. AVX2 variant unavailable in the bundled faiss wheel (see logs/app.log) so the generic loader is used.

files.purpose: Pickled Python object (~20MB) holding the document/chunk metadata (paths, chunk text, ids) alongside the FAISS index so retrieval can map vector hits back to source chunks.

terms.definition: A fixed-size overlapping slice of a source document (here ~800 chars, 120 overlap) that is embedded and indexed, and later fed as retrieved context to the LLM.

files.notes: Loading a pickle is arbitrary code execution; the FAISS_ALLOW_DANGEROUS_DESERIALIZATION gate (off by default in .env.example) controls whether index.pkl is deserialized. Logs show the index was loaded in the development environment with the gate enabled, and hybrid_retriever populated BM25 with 4031 chunks on 2026-08-03.

data_flow: Two independent pipelines converge here. (1) Scrape-to-corpus (Node.js, bvb_scraped_data/): crawler writes markdown/ (4738 files) and pdf/ (272 files) plus metadata; build_clean_data.mjs cleans/dedupes these and injects gap_fill/ enrichment (live_recovery + research docs) to emit the cleaned knowledge_base/ corpus (corpus/web + corpus/pdf + legacy_bvb) with metadata/documents.json, statistics.json, excluded.json; enrich_metadata.mjs and verify_kb.mjs finish/validate it; build_benchmark.mjs emits the 344-question evaluation benchmark. The cleaned corpus is the source from which the canonical Markdown (data/canonical_markdown/) is curated. (2) Index-build and runtime (Python, src/campus_helpdesk/): ingest.py / infrastructure/rag/canonical_index_builder.py reads knowledge_source_path=data/canonical_markdown, chunks it (rag_chunk_size=800), embeds with all-MiniLM-L6-v2, and writes chunks.jsonl plus the FAISS store at data/faiss (index.faiss + index.pkl + index-manifest.json); at /chat time hybrid_retriever loads these indexes (BM25 + FAISS) and retrieval/rerank/LLM latencies are recorded by scripts/measure_baseline_timing.py into logs/timing_*.json. Runtime writes: POST /chat feedback -> logs/user_feedback.jsonl; TTS -> outputs/*.wav; robot camera -> storage/snapshots/*.jpg; verify_project.py -> data/analytics/reports/*.json; robot/app logs -> logs/**. The evaluation runner consumes bvb_scraped_data/benchmark/benchmark_questions.json to score the system and emits comparison reports under evaluation/results/.
external_deps: Piper TTS (piper phonemize + ONNX runtime) for data/piper voice
risks: Secrets leakage: logs/ui_debug.log contains a live-looking OpenRouter API key (sk-or-v1-...) inside a full settings dump, and the committed verification report references D:\AUNTII paths.

Empty/placeholder artifacts in production paths: outputs/full_pipeline_en_q1.wav is 0 bytes and chunks/ is empty, while real chunk artifacts land at the repo root (chunks.jsonl ~19MB, embedding_metadata.jsonl ~47MB) — path confusion between the documented layout and the actual outputs.
Large binaries tracked in git: data/faiss/index.pkl (~20MB), index.faiss (~11MB), data/piper/*.onnx (~63MB) inflate the repo (.git ~900MB per CLAUDE.md).

Point-in-time knowledge: the corpus and benchmark encode facts (NAAC grade, NIRF ranks, fee figures, leadership) as published in mid-2026 and must be re-verified for later cycles; benchmark questions cite source_documents paths that must stay in sync with corpus rebuilds.
Benchmark contamination guard: benchmark_questions.json is explicitly TEST-ONLY ('Do NOT add it to the searchable corpus') — adding it to the RAG index would poison evaluations.
Pickle deserialization gate: loading data/faiss/index.pkl is arbitrary code execution, gated by FAISS_ALLOW_DANGEROUS_DESERIALIZATION which is enabled in the development environment logs.

Timing audit tradeoff: STEP5 cut total latency from ~17.4s to ~7.2s but several benchmark answers regressed to 'couldn't find verified information' (Q3/Q4/Q5/Q6/Q7) — the optimization may have traded completeness for speed.

Legacy/low-quality crawl data: bvb_scraped_data/misc.md and markdown/ contain scraped HTML-table residue, ad text, and 4000+ near-duplicate pages (only ~325 unique signatures); 95 scanned PDFs have no extractable text (no OCR).

Path drift between machines: the verification report and ui_debug.log reference D:\AUNTII\ (an earlier working copy) while the repo lives at D:\helpdesk — check tools and logs for stale absolute paths.
user_feedback.jsonl contains only synthetic test rows (all identical 'test_sess' records with a '[1]' citation artifact), so there is no real user-feedback signal yet.
